4. The defence case is that the suit land has duly been recorded in Khas Khatian of the Government for which the land has also been settled in a settlement case No. 728/74-75 but it has been cancelled for violation of the terms of agreement incorporated in the deed of settlement and brought the land again in Khas possession of the government. Both the trial court and the appellate court have found the title and possession of the plaintiff in the lend in question and ultimately passed the decree for declaration of title in favour of the plaintiff-appellant but single Bench of the High Court Division in a Civil Revision made the Rule absolute setting aside both the judgment of the appellate court as well as the trial court on the ground that courts below have not, at all, considered the evidence adduced by the parties where they have absolutely failed to prove the settlement of their predecessor-in-interest. 

 5. Mr. Sheikh Muhammad Serajul Islam the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-appellant submits that the plaintiff are the successive heirs of one Abdul Aziz who purchased the land in the year 1923 from the tenant of the Zemindar and since then they have been successively possessing the suit land which is enough to pass the decree for declarations of title ignoring the S.A. Khatian, admittedly recorded in the name of the Government. The learned Advocate further submits that S.A. Khatian since has no presumptive value, therefore, it is the duty of the Government to prove how the land in question has been recorded in Khas Khatian but unfortunately not a single piece of evidence has been adduced by the Government to prove the title in the land in question.
